sectionGuide.why: Every accuracy or reliability claim must name *what* is being evaluated. Without stable terms for agent, multi-agent system, workflow, and model, the same score can mean “the LLM answered correctly” or “the business process succeeded” — and gap analysis cannot compare like with like.
sectionGuide.wgUse: Canonical evaluation-object vocabulary for benchmarks, inventories, and evaluation envelopes. Each row should declare subject and scope rings. Candidate for export to Taxonomy WG shared objects. Reviewers comment on JSON in `s03-boundaries-*.json` before citing terms elsewhere.
sectionGuide.enables: Core properties and reliability dimensions attach to a declared object; grounding and failure attribution require an agent boundary; benchmark coverage maps per evaluation subject. Nothing downstream is well-defined until this section is settled.
sectionGuide.priorities: **P0** locks the evaluation-object vocabulary the narrative assumes (agent, MAS, workflow, evaluation subject). **P1** adds specification, trajectory, and scope-ring terms needed to reproduce a run but not to choose the object. Sign off P0 before core properties — if agent vs workflow is unsettled, later definitions cannot stabilize.

categories.relevance: Charter scope: name *what* is evaluated (agent, MAS, workflow) before any accuracy or reliability claim. Stops leaderboard model scores from standing in for business outcomes.
categories.wgUse: Shared subject column in benchmark inventories · evaluation envelope fields · Taxonomy WG upstream batches

terms.definition: A model together with its instructions, context assembly, tool access, memory use, and decision loop — evaluated as one unit for a task or session, including tool calls made on its behalf.
terms.scopeNote: Default evaluation subject for most ARWG work.
terms.literatureNote: Widely used in agent benchmarks (WebArena, tau-bench, SWE-bench) as the scored unit: model plus tools and session logic. Differs from 'model' in leaderboard-only settings.

terms.definition: The interface where external infrastructure meets agent-internal state — including model calls, tool results, retrieved knowledge, and memory. Used to decide whether a failure originated inside the agent or in the environment serving it.
terms.scopeNote: Establish infrastructure health before attributing a failure to agent reasoning.
terms.literatureNote: AAIF-specific attribution construct for separating agent-internal from environmental failures. Not a standard benchmark term; needed so infrastructure vs cognition failures can be separated.

terms.definition: The part of the system to which an accuracy or reliability claim applies. Every claim must name one subject: model, agent, multi-agent system, or workflow. Unqualified claims are ambiguous.
terms.scopeNote: Foundational boundary rule for ARWG evaluation and reporting.
terms.literatureNote: AAIF rule: every claim must name model, agent, MAS, or workflow. Benchmark papers often leave this implicit — a common source of gap-analysis error.

terms.definition: A single language or machine-learning model evaluated at one inference call boundary with fixed inputs, excluding tools, memory assembly, and multi-step agent logic.
terms.scopeNote: Smallest evaluation subject. Model metrics do not substitute for agent or system metrics.
terms.literatureNote: Standard in NLP leaderboards (MMLU, HELM). ARWG treats this as the innermost subject; agent-level scores are not interchangeable.

terms.definition: A set of agents that exchange messages and coordinate on a shared task, evaluated at the orchestration boundary for one session or workflow run.
terms.scopeNote: Accuracy and reliability claims must state whether they apply to final system output or to individual agent steps.
terms.literatureNote: Used in MAS benchmarks (MultiAgentBench, REALM-Bench). Coordination and joint outcome scoring vary; attribution remains weak in literature.

terms.definition: An end-to-end process that may include agents plus non-agent steps such as databases, APIs, rules, and human checkpoints. Judged on final process outputs unless evaluation scope says otherwise.
terms.scopeNote: ARWG evaluation subject: agents plus scored non-agent steps. Not the same as durable-execution or orchestration 'workflow' in Workflows & Process Integration — disambiguate in cross-WG text (see README Community vocabulary census).
terms.literatureNote: Divergent: AAIF 'workflow' = evaluation object (full deployed process). Workflows & Process Integration WG uses 'workflow' for durable execution engines — disambiguation required when citing this term alongside Workflows & Process Integration.
